_comment: Hooks in exec form (command + args) — the recommended form to avoid quoting and path issues on Windows. No shell is invoked. The `if` field filters by permission rule before spawning the process: without it, every edit to any file would pay for a JVM startup. The `guard` entries are the deliberate exception: territory is deny-by-default (`skill_classes` in .claude/schemas/extensions.json), so an `if` narrowing them to a path list would recreate the denylist hole they exist to close — a design run once wrote docker-compose.yml, which no forbidden-path list named. `guard write` returns immediately when no phase is open, which is every write outside a skill invocation. The `Bash` entry is the same deny-by-default check reached from the other side: every other enforcement here matches on a tool name, so a heredoc or a `sed -i` passed through none of them (lessons-learned-014 § 1). It carries no `if` for the same reason the `guard` entries don't, and for one more — a permission rule matches a command prefix, and `cat > file`, the spelling that was actually used, has no prefix that names the write. A target it cannot read literally is skipped in silence, so the cost of a false positive is bounded by design. The write matchers are one list: `format` and `check` used to match `Write|Edit` alone, which left a `MultiEdit` territory-checked but never boundary-checked or formatted (lessons-learned-014 § 2). On `Stop`, `guard sweep` is the backstop behind both write guards: it reads what changed on disk since the baseline `guard prompt` took, so it catches the shell spellings the parser cannot read — and it is git-shaped, so a path git ignores is never swept. `compose gate` is the same `composeReport()` `doctor` and the bare `compose` use, silent while healthy: the check existed and had simply never been run against a project, which is how a broker unreachable from the host shipped on day one (lessons-learned-014 § 13). Every entry launches the precompiled `.claude/hooks/ArchHook.jar` (`java -jar`), not the source: a source launch recompiled the whole file on every call, ~3.3 s against ~0.3 s. `schema` and `doctor` report a jar built from another version of `ArchHook.java`; `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java build` rebuilds it under the pinned JDK. `format` and `check` carry `if: Edit(**/*.java)` — both return at their first line for anything else, so the filter loses nothing. Path rules in `if` are matched only through `Edit(...)`/`Read(...)`, and `Edit` covers every built-in tool that writes a file, `Write` included — which is why no `if` here spells `Write(...)`. Design: .claude/decisions/0075-precompiled-hook-jar.md. The `build` entry exists in this repository only: an edit to `ArchHook.java` rebuilds the jar right away, through the source launch on purpose, so a source that no longer compiles reports its errors there instead of leaving the hooks on the old jar in silence. `extraKnownMarketplaces` registers .claude/mods/ as the `nerviz-mods` marketplace — a `directory` source with a relative path, so each mod loads in place, from the main checkout, once the folder is trusted — and `enabledPlugins` turns each mod on; the `Edit(.claude/mods/**)` entry runs `schema`, which judges a mod whole, from disk. A mod draws what these hooks decide and enforces nothing: it does not load in `claude -p`, VS Code, a cloud session or under `--safe-mode`. Design: .claude/decisions/0131-mods-in-architect-designer.md.
